svg.title: Flexible hosts: local or Docker
svg.desc: Each session runs on a Host you pick. You talk to the manager (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode), which starts workers through ensemble-session; workers use the same clients. The host-side Session harness owns their lifecycle. On the Local Host, tmux, a guard parents the client on your machine as you: not isolated, auto mode. On the Docker Host the session asks ensemble-broker to start and close its own container: isolated, so its client runs in yolo mode by default. The host harness controls the Docker guard, the container's main worker process and direct client parent, through one docker attach channel with heartbeats; its owner also maintains credentials. EOF or heartbeat loss ends the guard; close retries until container removal is confirmed. The broker's installed executable is root-owned. Once logged in, only the broker reads its own credential roots and records in the login keychain; published host Linear access-token entries have a separate ACL. The App key and Codex refresh token stay with the broker. At start it writes session credential copies to a tmpfs: GitHub installation tokens valid an hour and renewed; close attempts revocation, while replaced or unreadable tokens expire; a Codex access token without its refresh token; a Claude setup-token copy deleted with the container; a separately issued Linear role-app token only when declared; requested OpenCode provider API-key copies; and declared environment-secret files. Static copies disappear with the container. The workspace volume is kept across restart and resume. The worker cannot reach the host keychain, host Linear app tokens (a local board needs none), host gh login or Docker socket. Public worker traffic goes through the external egress proxy; the default workers policy denies local/LAN destinations except configured host:port exceptions. The worker clones, pushes and opens draft pull requests on GitHub as the App bot. Its code/workspace delivery to your machine uses GitHub; live output and client session state also return directly to the host.
